answer: Make standing depend on a sequential, memory-hard chain begun at dawn: each identity extends its own basalt-slow chain, every step depending on the last, and all chains are mapped in a public atlas. One honest chain runs at full speed, but a single operator running many chains in parallel thrashes the same memory, so each extra chain slows all of them superlinearly. Minting identities stays cheap; running them all at once is not, and a bought chain cannot be split without breaking its sequence.
